name: sound2text
description: Speech to text as five steps rather than one call. Reads the audio itself — RIFF, every PCM width, IEEE float, and the a-law/mu-law that comes off a phone line, decoded in numpy now that the stdlib has dropped audioop — resamples through a windowed-sinc polyphase filter, finds the speech with an energy-and-flatness detector that costs 80 ms a minute and no model, recalls anything transcribed before by the hash of the audio rather than its filename, routes to whichever recogniser is actually fastest or cheapest on this machine, and sends only what is left. The step that makes the trimming pay is packing: a Whisper encoder always sees thirty seconds, so eight two-second segments sent separately cost eight full windows — 43% slower than sending the untouched file, and 2.6x its word error rate, because a model handed two seconds of audio has no context and guesses. Packed back to fill the window, the same recording is sent with 48% less audio and comes back with a *lower* WER than the original file (0.086 against 0.111 on the bundled sample), the silence it was hallucinating words into having gone. On a local model that is what this module buys: accuracy. On a metered API it is the bill, which falls with the seconds uploaded. Five engines behind one interface (faster-whisper, transformers, whisper.cpp, and any OpenAI-shaped API), a stub that describes sound instead of pretending to transcribe it, and a number for every claim above.
frontend: src/app.py (stdlib — the console at /sound2text on :50641; proxies /sound2text/_api)
state: ~/.mod/sound2text — keys.json (0600), the transcript cache, and the speed ledger. Nothing private is ever written into this directory.

pipeline.decode: RIFF read here (pcm 8/16/24/32, float32/64, a-law, mu-law) → mono float32 16 kHz; ffmpeg or soundfile used only for containers this cannot open
pipeline.detect: energy against an adaptive noise floor + spectral flatness + hysteresis; ~80 ms per minute of audio, no model
pipeline.recall: sha256 of the samples, the engine, the model, the language and the task — per segment, so appending to a recording only costs the new part
pipeline.route: fast | cheap | best, scored on what each engine has actually done on this machine
pipeline.run: segments packed to fill the model window, then batched

engines.faster-whisper: CTranslate2 int8/float16 — the fastest local option; pip install faster-whisper
engines.whisper-torch: transformers + torch, CPU or GPU, batched — needs nothing but pip
engines.whisper.cpp: the CLI and a ggml model — no python dependencies at all
engines.stub: describes the sound instead of transcribing it; every result carries transcript=false, and the router will never choose it on its own

measured.host: 24-core CPU, no GPU, openai/whisper-tiny.en, best of three runs, model loading excluded
measured.harvard-8k.wav (33.6s, 86% speech): whole file 2 windows / 33.6s sent / 1.77s / WER 0.111 — trimmed 8 windows / 28.9s / 2.53s / WER 0.284 — trimmed+packed 2 windows / 29.7s / 1.72s / WER 0.086
measured.sparse (64.3s, 51% speech): whole file 3 windows / 64.3s sent / 1.44s / WER 0.148 — trimmed 8 windows / 32.6s / 2.17s / WER 0.296 — trimmed+packed 2 windows / 33.3s / 1.59s / WER 0.099
measured.the trap: trimming without packing is 43% slower than sending the untouched file and 2.6x the word error rate — a padded 30s window costs the same whether it holds 2s of speech or 28s
measured.what packing buys: on a local model, accuracy: the packed run beats the untouched file on WER in both files, because it removed the silence the model was hallucinating words into
measured.what trimming buys: on a metered API, the bill: 48% less audio uploaded on a recording that is half silence. It does not buy local wall-clock time, which tracks tokens generated, not seconds of file

endpoints.vad: POST /vad (upload) | GET /vad?path= — includes a waveform for drawing
endpoints.compare: GET /compare?path= — whole file vs trimmed vs packed
endpoints.keys: GET /keys | POST /keys | DELETE /keys/{vendor} — writes are loopback-only

toolchain.optional: any one recogniser (faster-whisper, transformers+torch, whisper.cpp, or an API key); ffmpeg only for containers other than WAV

samples.harvard-8k.wav: real speech, 33.6s, 8 kHz, 86% speech — the worst case for skipping, and the file to check that skipping never costs anything
samples.sparse-45pct-speech.wav: built by this module from the real one with room tone between the sentences; labelled as constructed everywhere it appears
